messages:
jordan: thinking out loud — can we try a watermark-based priority degradation at the edge? when memory or active-streams hit X% we demote low-priority requests to best-effort instead of outright rejecting. less noisy than hard rejects and keeps high-priority SLOs intact.

emily: hmm. idea sounds promising. what does 'demote' mean exactly here? drop streaming, reduce tokens, or switch model variant?

jordan: good Q. prototype idea: for demoted requests we
- convert long-poll/streaming to short-poll (truncate streaming window)
- reduce available token budget per request (soft cap)
- apply hedging only for critical routes, skip hedging for demoted ones

frank: tradeoffs: fair scheduling vs starvation. If demotion is sticky, some customers could see persistent degradation. Need a clear decay/rehab policy.

samir: agree. also instrumentation heavy: we must track demotion count, demotion duration per request-id, and p50/p95 delta for demoted vs normal. otherwise ops will be blind.

jordan: yep. thinking config knobs: soft_watermark (start demotion), hard_watermark (reject). rehab window: how long before a demoted session can be promoted again.

emily: can you paste a sample config sketch?

jordan: sure:
```yaml
edge.priority_degradation:
  soft_watermark: 0.68  # start demoting low-prio when memory used fraction >= 0.68
  hard_watermark: 0.92  # force hard-rejects above this
  demote_actions:
    - convert_streams_to_poll: true
    - per_request_token_cap: 512
    - disable_client_hedging: true
  rehab_seconds: 20
  per_route_override: true
```

frank: couple concerns:
- streams: converting to poll mid-request might break client UX and tool-calling. need graceful 101-style handshake or trailer telling client to reconnect in poll mode.
- token caps could bias prompt authors; might need intelligent token allocation (priority-weighted).

samir: operational plan suggestions:
- start with telemetry-only mode (emit demotion decisions but don't act)
- canary on non-critical routes (embeddings/small-chat) for 24h
- add abort/retry signals to SDKs so clients can react to demotion gracefully

emily: what about fairness across tenants? if one tenant floods, do we demote across all tenants or respect per-tenant quotas first?

jordan: priority: 1) enforce per-tenant reservation/quotas, 2) if global pool pressure persists, apply watermark demotion but prefer inter-tenant weighted fairness (demote proportionally by consumption).

frank: and SLA layers — premium customers should have an escape hatch (reserved capacity or higher watermark). map config to tiers.

infra-bot: NOTE: simulated load job #486 queued for 1776544300, will run 10m soak against canary cluster when triggered.

samir: followups/actions:
- jordan: write short RFC with config schema + implementation sketch + metrics list (demotion_rate, average_demote_duration, p50/p95 per-tier).
- emily: prototype client-side fallback UX for streaming->poll and ensure function/toolcall semantics preserve idempotency.
- frank: design rehab/decay heuristics and fairness allocator.
- ops: run infra-bot job on canary, capture memory/stream metrics.

jordan: will draft RFC by EOD tomorrow and attach a tiny sim that toggles soft/hard thresholds.

emily: ack. I can pair on the fallback UX tomorrow morning.

frank: +1. if we keep actions reversible and telemetry-first we should be safe to iterate.

samir: thanks all. if infra-bot posts results, ping this thread.
